## From a Tool to a Teammate

::: {.two-cards}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[A research team]{.card-title}

- Many agents, different roles, working together
- They propose, attack, verify, and re-check each other
:::
::: {.card .card-amber}
[A personal assistant]{.card-title}

- One agent that carries work across sessions
- Remembers context, uses your tools, acts on your behalf
:::
:::

::: {.explainer}
Draft outline --- the two shapes below are where agents pay off: a *panel* that pressure-tests ideas, and an *assistant* that just gets things done.
:::

## A Research Team {.section-divider}

## Many Roles, One Question

::: {.three-cards}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Debate]{.card-title}

- A proposer generates ideas; an adversary attacks them
- Disagreement surfaces the weak points early
:::
::: {.card .card-amber}
[Ground it]{.card-title}

- A verifier checks claims against your own library
- An analyst builds the data and runs the empirics
:::
::: {.card .card-teal}
[Check it]{.card-title}

- A replicator re-derives the result independently
- Two paths to the same number, or a red flag
:::
:::

::: {.explainer}
The `coauthor` skill orchestrates this. *[Placeholder: walk one round of propose --- attack --- verify.]{.accent}*
:::

## Personal Assistants {.section-divider}

## An Agent That Carries the Work

- Give it a goal, not a script; it plans the steps
- It uses tools --- files, code, the web --- to act
- State persists, so today's work builds on yesterday's
- *[Placeholder: a standing assistant for a recurring task]{.accent}*

## What Makes It an Agent

::: {.two-cards}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Not just answering]{.card-title}

- It decides *what to do next*, then does it
- It checks its own output and retries
:::
::: {.card .card-amber}
[Kept in bounds]{.card-title}

- You choose which tools it may use
- You review before anything irreversible
:::
:::

## Why This Belongs at the End {.centered-statement}

::: {.card .card-dark}
Everything so far was you [directing a tool.]{.accent} An agent is you [delegating a task]{.accent} --- which means the new skills are describing the goal well and judging the result.
:::

## Breakout {.section-divider}

## Questions to Discuss

- What recurring task would you hand to a standing assistant first?
- For a research question in your field, what roles would your ideal agent team have?
- What tools would you *withhold* from an agent working on real data?
- Where is the line between useful delegation and losing track of what was done?
